title: UMD Garden Crawl
hosts: University of Maryland Arboretum & Botanical Gardens
description_text: Explore and experience UMD’s Arboretum and Botanical Gardens. The UMD Garden Crawl invites Android smartphone users in the University of Maryland community to step outside and share the places that make UMD’s campus feel alive. From October 9–November 8, submit your discoveries using an experimental version of the Proofmode Android App, for a chance to win up to $1000 in gift cards and prizes through challenges while contributing to a trusted community-built record of UMD’s gardens. Photos captured with Proofmode include verifiable information about where and when they were taken, ensuring submissions are based on real experiences in real places. Qualifying Entries must be captured with Proofmode’s in-app camera (currently only available for Android users) during the event timeframe, within an approved garden submission zone, meet the event’s technical requirements, and pass internal review. There is no limit to the number of submissions you can make during the event; however, only qualifying entries count toward prize eligibility. Explore the submission zones on the UMD Garden Crawl Map. Ready to get started? Visit the UMD Garden Crawl Website for more information about the event, how to use Proofmode, and how to participate.

description_text: Join the University Career Center for an interactive workshop designed to help students strengthen their resumes for internships, jobs, and other career opportunities. Participants will review resumes section by section and learn strategies to improve formatting, bullet points, and overall content. Students are encouraged to bring a current resume and be ready to make real-time edits during the session. To prepare your best effort resume ahead of time, check out the following: Resume videos on our website that walk you through how to make a quality resume Resume samples on our website Our Resume Basics module that provides further insight Learning Outcomes By the end of the workshop, students will be able to: Identify the key sections of a strong resume and their purpose. Apply strategies to improve resume formatting, structure, and overall readability. Strength bullet points to better communicate skills, experiences, and accomplishments. title: SkillStorm: Tech Training and Client Deployment Programs
hosts: University Career Center & The Presidents Promise
categories: ThoughtfulLearning; Career Development; Audience: Undergraduate Students; Academic
description_text: Location: University Career Center, Hornbake South Wing 3135 Join John Tansill from SkillStorm to learn about 2 excellent opportunities for tech students that involve paid AI training and work with top federal and Fortune 100 clients. See program details below. This event is in 2 parts. Feel free to join one or both: 12-1 p.m. Overview of the 2 programs and their eligibility requirements. Pizza and beverages. 1-2 p.m. - John will stay to answer questions and talk 1:1 with students or in small groups. Programs Offered By SkillStorm: 1. TechForce By Design Screened by SkillStorm and the client company, selected candidates will enter a cohort for 12-14 weeks of tech training, based on the requirements of the client. The training can lead to certifications in software development, cybersecurity, cloud, data, AI, MML, and others. You will then work with the client to solve their tech challenges, working in collaboration with your cohort at SkillStorm. Communication skills are essential as you will be client-facing throughout this role. ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS: 1-3 years of tech experience including software development & programming. (1 year can be satisfied with 12 months of internship experience in a tech field.) Available for potential relocation Due to federal contract requirements, candidates must possess U.S. citizenship and be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance. 2. Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) Selected individuals are paid through their 6 weeks of tech training, then deployed to federal and Fortune 100 clients where they are embedded to build AI-powered solutions. Continuous mentorship, training and certification help build your capacity and your value to clients throughout your career. AI experience is not a criteria for selection but these skills will be built as you train and develop. ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS: Best for Master's students and alumni, as 3-5 years of experience in a tech field is required Available for potential relocation Due to federal contract requirements, candidates must possess U.S. citizenship and be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance Register on Handshake!

title: Hive Check
description_text: During this meeting we will visit our three hives to monitor their health as populations increase with the coming spring. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close-toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. Join our Discord for the most up-to-date information and announcements on event details. Also feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page or email for any questions you might have. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products into a variety of goods. The Beekeeping Club seeks to offer anyone with a curiosity or passion for bees and beekeeping the ability to participate in beekeeping regardless of their skill level or prior experience and to guide them in learning more about bees and the role beekeeping plays in a sustainable world.

title: Beyond the Professoriate Fall Watch Party Series: How to Research Career Options in Industry
categories: ThoughtfulLearning; Career Development; Audience: Graduate Students
description_text: Beyond the Professoriate, an e-learning platform available to all UMD doctoral students and postdocs, is hosting a series of live events throughout the fall semester. Can’t make the live sessions? Come grab a snack and watch the recordings with us! Discussion to follow! For access needs, accommodations and questions, please contact Dr. Kristyn Lue at kriselue@umd.edu --- About this session (from Beyond the Professoriate): One of the most common struggles PhDs face early in their job search is identifying nonacademic career options that feel like a genuine fit. With a highly specialized background, it can be difficult to know where to begin — or how to evaluate whether a career path aligns with your skills, values, and goals. But career exploration does not have to be an overwhelming process. With the right framework, you can identify career pathways that make sense for your background and take concrete steps toward your job search. Join the Beyond Prof team for this webinar where you'll learn how to begin identifying and researching nonacademic career options that align with your background and professional goals. This webinar is designed for doctoral students, PhDs, and postdocs from all academic disciplines who are wondering: Why is it so difficult to identify career options that align with my background and expertise? How do I research career options that fit my skills, values, and personal goals? Once I have identified career options, where do I begin my job search?

Participants will learn about the current job market, how to use campus and external resources to search effectively, and ways to stay organized throughout the process. The session will also cover strategies for making a positive impression through resumes and interviews, connecting with professionals in their field of interest, and identifying ways to gain relevant experience beyond traditional internships. Students will leave with practical tools to navigate their search with greater focus and confidence. Learning Outcomes By the end of the workshop, students will be able to: Identify trends and realities in the current job and internship market that may shape your search. Use campus and external resources to find internships, jobs, and other relevant opportunities. Develop strategies for organizing and managing your search effectively. Create one or two actionable next steps to move forward in their career development. This is especially the case in our current moment, as the job market is highly competitive and searches are taking longer than they have in recent years. description_text: Join the University Career Center for an interactive workshop designed to help students build confidence and prepare effectively for interviews. Students will learn about different interview formats, including phone, virtual, asynchronous, case, and technical interviews, with practical tips for approaching each. The session will focus especially on behavioral interviewing, including how to prepare for common questions, research an employer and role, and develop clear, compelling examples that highlight skills and experiences. Students will leave with strategies to feel more prepared, communicate their experiences effectively, and approach interviews with greater confidence. Learning Outcomes By the end of the workshop, students will be able to: Identify different types of interview formats and strategies for preparing for each. Recognize key information to research about an employer and position before an interview. Develop and organize “power stories” that clearly communicate your skills, experiences and strengths. NACE Career Readiness Competencies Through this workshop, students will develop the following NACE Career Readiness Competencies: Career & Self-Development Communication Professionalism Critical Thinking For any access needs, accommodations and questions, please contact the University Career Center at ucc–studenthelp@umd.edu or call 301.314.7225 Register using this link: https://careers.umd.edu/events/event-calendar/preparing-interviews-0

description_text: During this meeting we will visit our three hives to monitor their health as populations increase with the coming spring. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close-toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. Join our Discord for the most up-to-date information and announcements on event details. Also feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page or email for any questions you might have. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products into a variety of goods. The Beekeeping Club seeks to offer anyone with a curiosity or passion for bees and beekeeping the ability to participate in beekeeping regardless of their skill level or prior experience and to guide them in learning more about bees and the role beekeeping plays in a sustainable world.

description_text: Welcome to the UMD Campus Diwali Celebration 2026! The 14th Annual Campus Diwali Celebration, hosted by the BAPS Campus Fellowship (BCF), on Tuesday, November 17th, 2026. This festive event will take place at the Adele H. Stamp Grand Ballroom at the University of Maryland, running from 6:30 pm to 8:30 pm. Come join us for a night filled with vibrant colors, delicious food, and joyous festivities. Let's celebrate the festival of lights together with music, dance, and traditional performances. Don't miss out on the chance to experience the beauty of Diwali right here on campus! Get ready to immerse yourself in the rich culture and traditions of Diwali as we light up the night with divas and share in the spirit of togetherness. Whether you're a seasoned Diwali celebrator or new to the festivities, this event is sure to be a memorable experience for all. Mark your calendars and join us for a magical evening at the UMD Campus Diwali Celebration 2026! FREE FOOD | EXHIBITION | PERFORMANCES About BAPS CAMPUS FELLOWSHIP at UMD BAPS Campus Fellowship is a student organization recognized across 35 of the country’s largest universities. BCF is a dynamic organization dedicated to uniting students on campus and fostering a deeper understanding of Hindu heritage and culture. We achieve this through engaging group discussions, exciting campus events, and meaningful community service projects. BCF proudly operates with the approval of the Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, Inc. (BAPS), a denomination of the Hindu faith with millions of followers worldwide. Every year, we host a vibrant Diwali celebration, welcoming students and faculty from our campus. This event serves as a tribute to the values of Diwali, including unity, self-reflection, personal growth, rejuvenation, and compassion. The evening will feature enchanting musical performances, a thought-provoking exhibition, inspiring speeches, and traditional cuisine. In recent years, we have been honored to host 900+ attendees and have had the dedicated support of 50+ volunteers.

title: Hive Check
description_text: During this meeting we will visit our three hives to monitor their health as populations increase with the coming spring. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close-toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. Join our Discord for the most up-to-date information and announcements on event details. Also feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page or email for any questions you might have. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products into a variety of goods. The Beekeeping Club seeks to offer anyone with a curiosity or passion for bees and beekeeping the ability to participate in beekeeping regardless of their skill level or prior experience and to guide them in learning more about bees and the role beekeeping plays in a sustainable world.

title: Fall 1 Event
description_text: This is a general event to cover the operations of the Terrapin Rocket Team (TRT) during the Fall 1 application window. TRT is among the best collegiate rocketry team in the world. TRT has 3 major projects, they are IREC, Liquids, and High Altitude. The IREC team is the largest and their goal is to compete and win the International Rocketry Engineering Competition that takes place every year in Midland Texas. The team is broken up into Solids, which builds our custom rocket motor, Airbrake, which creates the airbrake for the rocket that opens up to we hit the exact altitude we are attempting, Payload, which builds the team's payload, Avionics which designs and builds all of the team's custom flight computers, and Aerostructures, which builds the airframe of the rocket and the parachutes. The goal of Liquids is to build the team's first ever liquid rocket engine and will compete in FAR-OUT in the Mojave desert this year. The goal of High Altitude is to break the altitude record of the team until we hit the legal limit for amateur rocketry of over 400,000 feet.

title: ASA Fall Ball 2026
description_text: The annual Fall Ball is a cultural event in which students, alumni, those interested in Africa, and supporters of the African Student Association join together to join in a night of entertainment, enlightenment, and fun. At this event, there is a fashion show segment as well as musical performances that especially highlight the different cultures within Africa. It is during this event that our Mr. and Ms. ASA are elected based on their talent by the audience and a panel of qualified judges based on their talent and answer. The proper dress attire for this event is formal wear. In addition, we will be serving cultural food during the course of performances/contests. The event is not restricted to Africans and we invite people of all races to enjoy African culture by enjoying our food, listening to our music, as well as supporting the local performers who will be showcasing their talents. In this show, we will incorporate performances and acts that are unique to African culture. These different performances and acts will embrace and showcase the different cultures in the east, west, north, and southern parts of our continent. This showcase will aim to revive African culture and show how our talents influence music and comedy all around the world. In addition, we aim to show the diversity that lies in Africa. The show entails social as well as educational components. The purpose of the Fall Ball is to educate and expose the University of Maryland community to the different aspects that define and characterize African culture. We aim to do this through musical and theatrical performances, a fashion show, and spoken word. The performances highlight the beats, instruments, and rhythm that make African music and dance so unique. The fashion show celebrates and displays the traditional attire of different African cultures and the fashion trends that are prominent amongst Africans. In addition, Fall Ball acts as the closing day of our annual Africa Week. This is a full week of African-related events leading up to the Fall Ball. The events during our Africa week are also open to all UMD students that are interested in African Culture. There are no other events of this magnitude on campus that are tailored to all African students so this event gives the African community on UMD a chance to allow their culture and academics intersect.

title: Beyond the Professoriate Fall Watch Party Series: Building a Network to Help You in Academia and Beyond
categories: ThoughtfulLearning; Career Development; Audience: Graduate Students
description_text: Beyond the Professoriate, an e-learning platform available to all UMD doctoral students and postdocs, is hosting a series of live events throughout the fall semester. Can’t make the live sessions? Come grab a snack and watch the recordings with us! Discussion to follow! For access needs, accommodations and questions, please contact Dr. Kristyn Lue at kriselue@umd.edu --- About this session (from Beyond the Professoriate): Networking is one of the most overlooked skills in a PhD job search. It is often seen as awkward, transactional, or evidence of "nepotism." But in practice, networking is how academics AND professionals build community. It is through community that academics and professionals find mentors, learn from others in their field, and stay informed about opportunities and areas of growth. Networking is also standard practice outside of academia, and an essential part of an effective job search — academic or nonacademic. The earlier you start building your network, the more it will work in your favor when opportunities arise. Join the Beyond Prof team for this webinar where we'll walk you through how to build and grow a network that supports your career goals, whether you are exploring careers in academia or beyond. This webinar is designed for doctoral students, PhDs, and postdocs from all academic disciplines who are wondering: How can networking help me in an academic or nonacademic job search? Where do I find people to connect with? How do I start if I have never done anything like this before?

title: The Why and How of Academic Conferences
categories: ThoughtfulLearning; Educational; Audience: Graduate Students; Academic
description_text: Presenting at academic conferences is a mainstay of an academic career. Conferences are places where you share early findings, get valuable feedback, and hone your communication skills. In this series, we’ll demystify the idea of going to a conference, starting with the why and how and then moving through the steps of writing an abstract, preparing a talk or a poster presentation, and refining your delivery, and being prepared to network. The Why and How of Academic Conferences: Understanding how to select a conference, how to submit an abstract, ways to fund your trip. What is a CFP? What’s the difference between submitting a poster or a paper? Can graduate students organize panels? How should I dress? Hear from a panel of graduate students about their experiences attending conferences.

title: Rich with Love: Closing Reception and Award Ceremony
description_text: Please join us for the closing reception and award ceremony (RSVP here) for Rich With Love: A Decade of Remembrance, an exhibition in partnership with the Bowie State University-University of Maryland Social Justice Alliance. As both campuses approach ten years since the loss of 1st Lt. Richard W. Collins III, this exhibition honors Lt. Collins’ life, legacy, and humanity while creating space for collective reflection on love, loss, justice, belonging, and remembrance. Too often, acts of racial violence reduce individuals to headlines, statistics, or symbols. This exhibition includes artworks which resist that erasure by centering the fullness of life, memory, and human connection. Rich with Love is both a remembrance and an invitation, an interrogation of how we bear witness to violence without allowing it to define the lives taken, and how art can function as a tool for healing, truth-telling, and social transformation. The exhibit takes inspiration from "Rich with Love: A Mini-Documentary on 1st Lt. Richard W. Collins III", which can be watched on YouTube and in the gallery during the exhibition. The artworks in this exhibition were contributed by community members from Bowie State University, the University of Maryland, College Park, and beyond. As part of this exhibition, the selection committee, composed of representatives from the Collins family, Bowie State University, and the University of Maryland will select three pieces to receive a cash award: $500 for first place, $350 for second place, and $200 for third. The award winners will be announced at the closing reception on Thursday, December 10. Rich with Love will be on view from October 15 to December 12, 2026, and it features Isabella Akilo, Tracy L. Barwick, Dr. Cristophoros Allen Beck, Taylor Brown, Charles W. Clark, Demere Coker, Laurine Dzossou-Mawule, Stevener Gaskin Jr., Diana Gonzales, Susan Harkins, Isabella Harvey, Micah Harvey, Alexis Hunter, Kate Izsak, Joshua Lee, Leah F. Lubin, b.a. medina, Elaine Rudder, Leon Timbo, Art Vidrine, Toni Pierce Webb, Ishtaire Worthy, Cadets from the University of Maryland, Bowie State and University of Maryland Students, Faculty, and Staff. ABOUT THE BOWIE STATE UNIVERSITY-UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND SOCIAL JUSTICE ALLIANCE The BSU-UMD Social Justice Alliance (SJA) is a collaborative initiative between Bowie State University, the University of Maryland, and the 2nd Lieutenant Richard W. Collins III Foundation, established to honor Lt. Collins’ legacy and advance racial and social justice across our campuses and communities. Led by faculty and staff across both institutions, the SJA brings together students, educators, and community members through curricular initiatives, experiential learning, and public programming to bridge communities, deepen dialogue, and translate learning into meaningful, collective action for social change. ABOUT THE STAMP GALLERY Located on the first floor of the Adele H. Stamp Student Union—Center for Campus Life at the University of Maryland, College Park, the Stamp Gallery is dedicated to exhibiting contemporary art, especially the work of emerging and mid-career artists. The Stamp Gallery supports contemporary art that is challenging, academically engaging, and attuned to broad community and social issues. Through meaningful exhibitions and programming, the Gallery offers outside-of-the-classroom experiential learning opportunities. It functions as a laboratory where emerging artists and curators experiment and work through their ideas. The Gallery’s programming aims to emphasize the importance of process to contemporary artistic practice and to provide a forum for dialogue. FREE and open to the public. Gallery hours: Mondays–Thursdays: 10 am – 8 pm, Fridays: 10 am – 5 pm, Saturdays: 11 am – 5 pm, Sundays: Closed. More information: stamp.umd.edu/gallery

Although the volunteering takes place at a church it is not religious but is rather focused on art and forming connections with the kids. We meet at the UMD Memorial Chapel every Tuesday at 2 PM to carpool to the church. We are always in need of more volunteers!

title: LTSC Power Hour
hosts: Office of Letters and Sciences; STRONG Connections
categories: ThoughtfulLearning; General Interest Meeting; Educational; Audience: Undergraduate Students; Academic; Social; Networking
description_text: LTSC Power Hours are bi-weekly study halls designed for Letters and Sciences (LTSC), Freshmen Connection (FC), and Academic Achievement Program (AAP) students to get things done and connect with others. Bring your assignments, grab a seat, and use the time to study, socialize, meet other students, or get help from an academic advisor. Each Power Hour will also feature rotating special guests—including BMGT and STEM advisors—to help students navigate major applications, explore academic options, and get answers to their questions. All are welcome, every week! Fall Schedule September 8 September 22 - CMSC App help October 6 - BMGT App help October 20 November 3 November 17 December 1 December 15

title: High Altitude Subteam Meeting
description_text: This is the weekly meeting for the High Altitude sub-team meeting. High Altitude is focused on building the technology that will help the team to break altitude records and eventually go to space. These meetings are weekly and open to anyone that would like to join.

title: Christian Science Organization (CSO) Meeting
description_text: At CSO meetings, we usually share short readings one of us puts together from the Bible and Science and Health with Key to the Scriptures by Mary Baker Eddy. Reading and studying ideas and concepts in the Christian Science Weekly Bible Lesson is another option. As always, questions about anything are welcome for conversation and sharing....the hour goes by quickly!

title: Liquids Sud-team Meeting
description_text: This is the weekly Liquids sub-team meeting. The goal of Liquids is to build a rocket the is powered by a custom liquid bi-propellant engine. This is the state of the art for powerful rockets like the Saturn-V and the core stage of NASA's SLS.

title: En Camino
location: Langley Park Community Room off of Merrimac Drive
description_text: En Camino con la Comunidad is a weekly service opportunity for University of Maryland students. Students are transported by van from campus to a community center in Langley Park. University students tutor and mentor elementary school children (pre-k to 6th grade) for several hours. Volunteers help the children with homework, reading, workbooks, crafts and games. We are always looking for more volunteers! We meet at the Memorial Chapel each Wednesday and travel together to the community.

title: CARing
location: Hope Lutheran Church 4201 Guilford Dr, College Park, MD
description_text: The Thursday CARing Kids program is a weekly service opportunity for University of Maryland students. The program seeks to provide role models to the elementary school children of Langley Park. This program pairs each child one-on-one with a university student, who is their buddy for the semester. CARing buddies focus on developing the children's language, reading, and math as well as their self image and social abilities which includes playing games and other recreational activities. We meet at Hope Lutheran Church just off campus each Thursday. We are always looking for more volunteers!

title: Wags for Wellness: Friday Visits at McKeldin Library
hosts: Health Promotion & Wellness Services; University of Maryland Libraries
categories: Health/Wellness; Audience: Open to All; Social
description_text: Wags for Wellness is an Animal Assisted Activity, featuring well trained and highly skilled volunteer pups from our partner organization People. Animals. Love. (PAL). Each team consists of at least one dog and one human, all of whom provide love, connection, companionship, and stress relief to the campus community. These visits can also serve as a great outlet for emotional wellbeing for students who may be missing their childhood or family pets.
